scars-of-kalakar/lore/0---the-lost-era/0.filePath: Scars of Kalakar/Lore/0 - The Lost Era/0000-00-00.md
scars-of-kalakar/lore/0---the-lost-era/0.content:
Molania, a barren wasteland akin to Mars, beckoned the Lost Ones with the promise of transformation. The mission commenced with hope, as domed cities dotted the planet’s surface, each acting as a crucial node for the colossal Terran Incubator. However, fate had other plans.
Molania’s long, hot days made it a haven for solar farms—until the sandstorms struck. A meteor had struck the planet, disrupting the weather.
The relentless storms ravaged the solar panels, rendering them obsolete and plunging the SEED into a state of desperation. Communication lines fell silent, and the grand vision of Terra-forming crumbled.
Daylight ceased to exist. A neighboring planet’s orbit cast an unrelenting shadow, blocking the star’s life-giving warmth. Panic stirred, but scientists reassured that it would pass within months.
Desperation led to a grim decision: the order was given to the robotic servants to decommission the project. The planet, once alive with ambition, fell into an eerie stillness.
There were no cries, there were no screams, just silence. Then darkness.
1642-04-01

scars-of-kalakar/lore/1---discovery-era/.content:
Sapient races encounter each other for the first time
The mythos is that a Kalakain shot a Toulikour and heard him cry out. While tending to the wound, they spoke of each others nation and vowed to meet each other’s village.
Reality: Kalakains when leaving the desert, were heading out to conquer the lands, believing it was their right as anEmpirialist society.  They came across other villages, and were surprised they could communicate. At first they believed other Kalakains domesticated and taught these species. Realizing they fooled themselves, they make treaties to trade, otherwise they will go to war.
Elegin, Toulikour,  Junkofuya, Burlian, Kralerian, Drengar, Muri and Kalakain all join the treaty
1652-06-10

Kingdom of Kalakar established
Capitalist Economy
First coinage (Silver)
the Kingdom of the Kalakains stood as the first great civilization, a beacon of unity that brought together a multitude of cultures, naming the lands after themselves; Kalakar. They established the earliest trade routes, weaving a network of commerce that spanned from East to West.
They also were able to use the plentiful hot springs for steam power, launching into the first Great Civilization.
The Elegin, wise in the ways of nature, worked as advisors.
The Kalakains, viewing themselves as superior to other races, sowed the seeds of their own downfall. Greed and corruption seeped into the heart of their society, eroding the foundations of their empire from within. Despite the grandeur of their open roads facilitating trade, the kingdom ultimately crumbled under the weight of its own hubris.
1692-11-29

A member of the king’s advisors wanted to sell cheap tonics and potions, but could not compete with Esprit Magi. He began a PR campaign to get it banned, stating its unnatural, witchraft, and makes people careless. Kalakains believing Esprit Magi is against nature through propaganda, outlawed performing Esprit Magi. This caused the Elegin to retreat to the west, and separate from the kingdom.
1693-09-17

With poor quality medicines, sold at exorbitant prices. Disease begins to spread fast. Famine spreads as farmers catch sick. Over time trust in the Court wears thin.
1703-01-04

Kalakains in a final cling to power, declares martial law and control of the Kingdom, and removes all other races from advisory roles.
1713-02-06

Greed and corruption caused even Kalakains to disregard the court, and the Kingdom loses the last of its power. Merchants continue to use trades routes established and slowly rise to power.
1718-06-07
1718-08-07

scars-of-kalakar/lore/2--guilded-age/171.content:
Merchants create the first Guild, followed by a craftsman guild, and an engineering guild. The Guilds rise in power and status, with the Merchant Guild being the strongest.
Barter economy, with prices set by the guilds each month. Leads to a Fraternist society.
1733-11-02

scars-of-kalakar/lore/2--guilded-age/173.content:
Drengar, feeling discriminated by the guilds, extorted by price gouging, and being underpaid, due to their size and intelligence, go into isolation.
Economically, this causes a famine the guilds try to hide as there are no Drengar to till the fields, or other hard labors.
The bakers begin using sawdust in the bread, engineers used iron nails instead of steel,
1753-10-02

scars-of-kalakar/lore/2--guilded-age/175.content:
Desperate, the guilds reach out to the Elegin where they share their technology of farming, irrigation, and wells. Saving the continent from famine.
The Elegin, having been in isolation, opens their borders for the first time, allowing trade of textiles and spices.
The economy moves to a gold based economy.
1762-09-30

scars-of-kalakar/lore/2--guilded-age/176.content:
Burlians angry at being cheated by the Junkofuya craft guilds, raids territory/tradepost ran by the guild.
The merchant guild ignored the Junkofuya as they were the weapon makers, and should be able to defend themselves.
1767-03-16

Burlians and Junkofuya are in a stalemate. The Burlians are adaptive hunters, and got used to the jungle. Using guerrilla tactics, the Junkofuya are forced into the swamp lands of the highly territorial Drengar.
1767-08-14

Fighting a two front war, the Junkofuya are nearly driven to extinction. Their population shrank from 400,000 to nearly 50,000 accounted for.
1768-01-01
Toulikours, a nation of warriors, decided they were weighed down by too much bureaucracy and dissolved their government. They decide to become nomads and mercenaries.

the Rastarians, driven from their mountainous homeland by overcrowding and dwindling resources, descended into the lowlands. Viewed as outsiders and treated akin to gypsies, as they brought new diseases, they soon fell under the yoke of the Kalakains, who captured and enslaved them.
Seeking refuge and protection, the Rastarians forged an alliance with the Drengar, offering priceless gems in exchange for their security. They form the KOA
Meanwhile, the Elegin Toulikour and Junkofuya entered into a pact named Waron to defend against any potential aggression from the KOA forces, ensuring a fragile balance of power in the region.
1772-05-13

scars-of-kalakar/lore/2--guilded-age/177.content: Rastarian Consulate member is assassinated by Empirialists

Rastarians raid Kalakain villages in retaliation. Waron refuse to act as to not battle KOA
Aberdine Salazar Abacus is kidnapped from his village.

It took minute for the word of the atrocities to reach Dmascus Maktar, Pharoah of the Elegin.
Ha Ven Maktar pleads to his father Dmascus Maktar to fight, but is jailed
Word reaches the Burlian army, and they join the KOA

scars-of-kalakar/politics/ideologies/cul.title: Cult of Ha Ven
scars-of-kalakar/politics/ideologies/cul.content:
A cult that worships the heroism of Ha Ven Maktar. They believe he guides their way through his unfettered guidance, and was a Martyr in the Great War, and he has risen again to end their fear. They see his father, and those who follow Abacus as heathens who follow the ego and selfishness. 
They make public shrines to him by remaking his sword out of scrap and lighting it on fire.

scars-of-kalakar/politics/ideologies/emp.title: Empirialist
scars-of-kalakar/politics/ideologies/emp.content: Kalakains who believe they are the true ruling class. All others are for the benefit of the elites.

scars-of-kalakar/politics/ideologies/fra.title: Fraternist
scars-of-kalakar/politics/ideologies/fra.content: The general belief that everyone has a role in society.

scars-of-kalakar/politics/ideologies/iso.title: Isolationist
scars-of-kalakar/politics/ideologies/iso.content: The belief that each race should never coincide socially, with the exception of bartering. No money as that incorporates other cultures.

scars-of-kalakar/politics/ideologies/pro.title: Proclivist
scars-of-kalakar/politics/ideologies/pro.content: The general belief that some races are different classes in society based on intelligence, economic productivity.
